messages:
olivia_support: FYI a customer just escalated — their ingestion pipeline started failing after the release at ~11:05. They say the 'order.items' field used to be an array and is now coming back as an object.

miguel_se: Can you drop the exact request + response they saw?

olivia_support: Pasting sanitized example from the customer:
```http
POST /v1/generate 
Content-Type: application/json
{
  \"model\": \"redwood-gen-1\",
  \"prompt\": \"Return the order as JSON matching schema: { order_id: string, items: [{id: string, qty: int}] }\",
  \"format\": \"json\"
}
```
Response they got:
```json
{
  "order_id": "ORD-8321",
  "items": {
    "0": { "id": "sku-11", "qty": 2 },
    "1": { "id": "sku-42", "qty": 1 }
  }
}
```

miguel_se: Ugh — array became an object keyed by index. That will break our customer's parser. When did the rollout happen?

deploy-bot: Release redwood-gen-1:v2026.03.11-flip deployed to production at 2026-03-11T11:04:55Z (canary 10% -> 100% completed).

ashley_pm: Is this limited to redwood-gen-1 or any model that hit the new formatter change? We need scope.

miguel_se: I ran a quick repro locally against v2026.03.11 image and saw same thing with deterministic seed. Looks like the JSON formatter component started normalizing arrays into index-keyed objects when top-level container ambiguity exists. Possibly due to new post-processing pass that canonicalizes maps/arrays.

sam_engineer: Repro steps I used:
```bash
# simple curl repro
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '{"model":"redwood-gen-1","prompt":"Serialize this order as JSON: items is an array","format":"json"}'
```
Got same object-shaped items. Also tried setting `format_options": { "force_array": true }` and the runtime ignored it.

olivia_support: Customer impact: their downstream parser is strict; they reported 12% of orders failing and queued. They want rollback or a hotfix.

miguel_se: Marking P1. Assigning to eng-runtime. Sam, can you capture a minimal test and add to regressions suite? Also capture model and postproc diffs.

sam_engineer: On it. I opened an internal ticket: RINF-2419. Added failing sample and a unit test that asserts arrays remain arrays when schema expects arrays.

ashley_pm: Communicated to customer that we're investigating and will provide ETA within 2 hours. Thanks for quick grab. :heart:

deploy-bot: Hotfix candidate branch created: fix/array-canonicalization-2419. CI green for unit tests.

miguel_se: If hotfix looks safe, prefer patching postproc and doing a 50% canary first. Avoid full rollback if we can verify fix is backward compatible.

olivia_support: Customer asked for timeline. I'll update them: 50% canary in ~90 mins, full rollout after validation.

sam_engineer: Sharing minimal diff in ticket — essentially skip index-keying when container matches schema array type. Pushed PR for code review.

ashley_pm: Thanks — please @miguel_se and @olivia_support when canary hits so CS can confirm customer's pipeline.

olivia_support: Will do. Customer appreciates the rapid response.

sam_engineer: Follow-up: added extra logging to capture original token stream for failing cases so we can trace why parser flipped shape.
